findings.evidence: vscode-extension/src/controller/workspace-controller.ts:260-276 grants workspaceWrite over the entire repository during implementation, verification, and review. vscode-extension/src/controller/approval-broker.ts:14-44 applies declared-path scope only to file-change approval requests and classifies commands using startsWith plus a narrow deny regex; for example, `git status; git clean -fd` is classified read-only, while git clean/restore/rebase, interpreters, redirection, and many PowerShell writers remain eligible. cutover.py:59-68 removes the legacy hook without installing a V2 task-scope execution guard. workspace-controller.ts:187-194 closes a run without interrupting an already writable turn.
findings.recommendation: Enforce realpath-safe current-task paths at the sandbox or mandatory execution-hook boundary, parse argv structurally, reject commands whose effects cannot be proven in scope, and interrupt/await the active turn before cancellation closes the run.
findings.title: Task scope is not enforced at the execution boundary

findings.evidence: .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/plan_store.py:25-30 and 63-92 protect load/check/replace only with threading.RLock. The MCP process constructs its own store at mcp_server.py:114-117, while the separate host process constructs another through host_bridge.py:109-113 and host_operations.py:23-35. Both processes can read revision N, pass the same expected revision, and atomically replace revision N+1; the later replace silently discards the earlier mutation.
findings.recommendation: Use a repository-scoped interprocess lock or durable compare-and-swap transaction covering read, revision check, and replace, then test simultaneous host and MCP mutations in separate real processes.
findings.title: Canonical ExecPlan mutations can lose cross-process updates

findings.evidence: .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/mcp_server.py:114-117 constructs RunService(repository) directly, leaving verification_engine unset. run_service.py:212-223 therefore rejects every production verification_run call as not configured. tests/test_v2_mcp.py:139-150 injects an engine manually, while lines 154-164 explicitly exercise the real run_stdio composition only for protocol discovery.
findings.recommendation: Construct the MCP service through build_run_service with strict schema-v2 configuration and add a process-level mcp-serve test that executes verification_run against the staged post-cutover project.
findings.title: The production MCP verification tool is permanently blocked

findings.evidence: verification_engine.py:265-274 defines evidence_is_current but it has no production caller. run_service.py:242-250 stores only aggregate status, IDs, and plan digest; task_update at 179-210 does not invalidate proof; completion_request at 259-276 and acceptance at 351-379 check only the stored passed flag. Thus code can change or tasks can complete after verification and still pass acceptance. Additionally, verification_engine.py:117-149 defaults release=False, run_service.py never supplies release=True, and cli.py:36-44/118-133 exposes no release mode, so staged release_only package, smoke, and app-server commands cannot run through the promised post-cutover V2 verify surface.
findings.recommendation: Bind every gate to a freshly recomputed source/output, plan, executable, and command-definition digest; invalidate proof after relevant mutations; recheck it at completion and acceptance; and expose an authorized release verification mode that runs the complete release-only matrix.
findings.title: Verification gates accept stale and incomplete proof

findings.evidence: git_transaction.py:51-100 defines scoped commit_slice, but no production path calls it. host_operations.py:16 exposes only five methods, and run_service.py:179-210 marks tasks completed without committing. Acceptance at run_service.py:351-379 marks the plan completed without calling PlanStore.complete. host_operations.py:56-62 resumes by doctor plus plan load only, without verifying current branch, recorded base ref, dirty state, or run ownership; run_start at 44-54 switches branch before the complete draft is validated, preserving an orphan branch on later failure.
findings.recommendation: Integrate GitTransaction and plan archival into task/gate completion, verify run branch and immutable base before every resume and mutation, validate the complete draft before switching, and preserve explicit recovery state for partial branch, staging, commit, or archive failures.
findings.title: Required Git commit, resume, and archival lifecycle is not integrated

findings.evidence: vscode-extension/src/controller/review-coordinator.ts:60-77 reports passed whenever parsed findings contain no open critical; lines 98-103 silently discard every text line not beginning with CRITICAL, WARNING, or ADVISORY. Therefore malformed output, an unavailable verdict, or ordinary prose describing a critical defect yields zero findings and passes. app-server/session.ts:316-351 accepts any nonempty bound agentMessage after turn completion as the compatibility review result. run_service.py:406-423 validates only client-supplied detached/thread/round/boolean fields and does not validate a structured verdict, source binding, or review provenance.
findings.recommendation: Require a strict versioned review envelope with explicit result, severity, findings, source/diff fingerprint, and thread/turn provenance; treat missing, malformed, unavailable, or contradictory output as blocked; verify the persisted envelope server-side.
findings.title: Detached review parsing fails open

findings.evidence: cutover.py:154-163 records prepared_from_head and base_ref in the approved manifest, but _preflight at 240-307 never compares either value with current Git state and never verifies the authorized branch or cleanliness. apply at 194-231 can consequently delete hundreds of allowlisted files after unrelated non-manifest source changes or on another compatible branch. Exact manifest-hash approval authenticates the manifest contents but not the checkout to which it is applied.
findings.recommendation: Immediately before the first mutation, require the authorized run branch, exact prepared_from_head, unchanged recorded base ref, and a clean tree except explicitly hash-bound finalizer artifacts; bind the reviewed source fingerprint and completion record into that same preflight.
findings.title: The destructive finalizer ignores its frozen HEAD and branch

findings.evidence: state.json TASK-012 still references EVID-018 through EVID-027 and says 64/64, while acceptance and current proof use EVID-035 through EVID-044 and 68/68. transition_record.py:58-59 and 170-214 correctly select current last_verification and the single current review, so this does not itself authorize stale proof. EVID-044.json:20 has raw_log null and retains only hashes/summaries for the current package, smoke, and UI proof.

findings.title: Transition audit records contain stale and inexact traceability

findings.evidence: vscode-extension/src/controller/workspace-controller.ts:349-361 converts each declared glob to its static directory prefix before supplying writableRoots; for example src/foo*.ts grants the src directory rather than only matching files. vscode-extension/src/controller/approval-broker.ts:55-71 performs lexical resolve/relative checks but no filesystem realpath, symlink, or junction containment check. docs/security.md:24 promises post-resolution workflow-path checking. Current unit evidence asserts emitted policies, while EVID-046/EVID-055 exercised a read-only live turn with zero authorized writes, so no real app-server test proves sibling, glob-expansion, or symlink escape denial under workspaceWrite.
findings.recommendation: Do not translate file globs into broader writable directories. This conflicts with requirements.md REQ-006 and AC-006/AC-007, design.md's requirement that slice commits stage declared paths plus ExecPlan, and AC-022 recovery expectations. The completed canonical plan can therefore remain untracked/dirty and is not recoverable from the asserted phase commits.

Commit the completed archive transition, verify commit_ref points to the checkpoint containing the recorded state, and test crash recovery, repository loss reconstruction, archive tracking, and clean preflight for the next run.

findings.evidence: vscode-extension/src/controller/task-scope.ts:54-86 accepts every existing physical non-reparse directory/** declaration and has no protected-root or protected-descendant rule. .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/contract_utils.py:142-159 and plan_contracts.py:39-51 likewise admit declarations such as .git/**, .devweave/runtime/**, docs/exec-plans/**, or docs/**. workspace-controller.ts:298-302 passes the resulting directory directly as a workspaceWrite root, while approval-broker.ts:27-37 uses the same permissive resolver. Consequently .git/** can expose repository metadata, and docs/** includes docs/exec-plans where the host's canonical plan resides; direct task writes can bypass the host-only Gate/state and Git-command boundaries. EVID-059 covers widened globs, traversal, ADS, NUL, and a junction escape, but contains no protected-root or protected-descendant case.
findings.recommendation: Define fail-closed protected physical roots for Git metadata, runtime journals/locks/cache, and canonical ExecPlan authority, and reject any declaration whose writable subtree equals, lies inside, or contains one of them. Enforce the rule in the plan contract and shared resolver before starting workspaceWrite. Add tests for .git/**, .devweave/**, docs/exec-plans/**, and ancestor declarations such as docs/**, proving both sandbox and file-approval denial without relying on undocumented sandbox exclusions.
findings.title: Task sandbox can still include Git and canonical host-authority paths

findings.evidence: .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/run_git_coordinator.py:237-258 creates the commit, then updates the deterministic ref, verifies content, and only afterward durably records committed journal state. For an intent journal, recovery at :233-249 accepts only the original HEAD or its immediate matching child. A crash after commit or update-ref followed by any later checkpoint makes that reconciliation impossible. assert_resume_target at :64-80 checks only journal branch agreement; HostFacade.run_resume at host_facade.py:41-46 then loads and returns the working plan without reconciling pending intents, resolving recorded task/Gate/archive refs, comparing checkpoint bytes, or restoring a missing plan. PlanStore.load at plan_store.py:56-68 simply fails when both working copies are absent. tests/test_v2_git_export.py:174-201 covers a crash after state replacement but before commit, while :255-257 deletes an archive and manually reads Git bytes rather than exercising runtime resume/restore. This does not establish docs/product.md:40 and :85's promised ref resolution, interrupted-mutation replay, and lost-working-plan recovery. cutover_provenance.py:130-138 also checks checkpoint fields only for non-emptiness.
findings.recommendation: Make resume run an authority-locked recovery pass before exposing the plan or accepting another mutation. Reconcile every intent using the deterministic ref and exact allowed tree diff even when HEAD has advanced, finalize or fail closed on all outstanding journals, resolve and validate every recorded task/Gate/archive ref and journal digest, and restore a missing active/completed plan from the latest valid checkpoint through an explicit atomic recovery path. Add fault injection after commit, after update-ref, after journal write, and after archive move; then advance HEAD/restart and prove one commit, valid refs, exact canonical bytes, functional lost-plan restore, and a clean next-run preflight.
findings.title: Checkpoint recovery remains incomplete across the commit-to-journal crash boundary

### AC-003: MCP allowlist and guard
Expose exactly eight tools and reject unknown, stale, malformed, traversal, or out-of-scope calls without state mutation.

### AC-004: Host/agent capability isolation
Allow only the authenticated host to start/resume runs, resolve decisions, decide Gates, or cancel.

### AC-005: Risk matrix
Require plan; plan plus acceptance; or scope plus design plus acceptance for low, standard, and high risk respectively, with matching review depth.

### AC-006: Git lifecycle
Reject dirty/detached/colliding starts and otherwise create a fixed-base run branch whose task/Gate/archive commits include the post-transition canonical plan, with no remote/merge/reset/switch-back side effect.

### AC-007: ExecPlan restart
Resolve saved task/Gate/archive checkpoint refs into equivalent canonical snapshots and replay an interrupted mutation without duplicating state transitions or commits.

### AC-008: Pending decision round-trip
Resolve only a valid option or allowed custom answer at the current revision; cancellation or malformed/stale input leaves the task pending.

### AC-009: Docs truth contract
Reach architecture, product, reliability, security, quality, and ExecPlan authority from the root map within bounded hops, with no broken links or duplicate canonical topic.

### AC-010: V1 export determinism
Produce byte-stable export artifacts for the recorded 21 work items and 411 evidence files without modifying V1 inputs.

### AC-011: CLI/schema contract
Keep six verbs and five strict public schema envelopes stable across valid, unknown-field, invalid-version, and malformed fixtures.

### AC-012: Rich client state coverage
Render and operate every key lifecycle state from scripted app-server events without calling a projection authoritative.

### AC-013: Verification safety parity
Select deterministic DAG stages, serialize writers, disable shells, enforce declarations, and admit only current zero-exit reconciled evidence.

### AC-014: Bounded independent review
Use detached reviewer identity; run one standard review or no more than three high-risk fix/reverify rounds, then block unresolved critical work.

### AC-015: Clean 2.0.0 package
Align public versions, generate but do not track VSIX output, and remove V1 runtime/UI mutation surfaces while retaining export recovery.

### AC-016: Adversarial authorization
Reject unknown methods, forged roles, stale revisions, traversal, symlink/junction escape, scope violations, and task globs that cannot map exactly to directory-subtree sandbox roots before repository/process mutation.

### AC-017: Deterministic state
Produce identical canonical snapshots/hashes from identical ordered transcripts and recover atomically around injected write failures or duplicate delivery.

### AC-018: Telemetry privacy
Redact secrets, bound payloads, omit prompts/reasoning, and keep unavailable usage null without estimates.

### AC-019: Mechanical architecture checks
Pass the healthy repository and report concrete code/path failures for oversized modules, reverse dependencies, long root guidance, schema drift, broken links, and untraced acceptance.

### AC-020: UI evidence bundle
Produce bounded DOM/accessibility/log/screenshot evidence with run, commit, Codex version, and protocol schema provenance.

### AC-021: Certification boundary
Mark only the executed Windows x64/VS Code matrix certified and label all other environments unverified.

### AC-022: Recovery drill
Identify the last current phase, source-only diff, evidence, export, and canonical-plan checkpoint after injected state/commit failure; recover a lost working plan from Git while leaving the base ref and remotes untouched.

findings.evidence: .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/contract_utils.py:173-200 performs only lexical protected-root comparison, and the current parser accepts `docs/EXEC-P~1/**`. vscode-extension/src/controller/task-scope.ts:77-95 checks protected authority before realpath, then checks the resolved root only for repository containment and emits it as writableRoots; workspace-controller.ts:298-302 supplies that root to workspaceWrite. On this certified NTFS checkout, `dir /x docs` maps `EXEC-P~1` to `exec-plans`; lstat reports an ordinary directory and realpath resolves it to the protected canonical `docs/exec-plans` root. tests/test_v2_contracts.py:68-84 and vscode-extension/test/unit/workspace-controller.test.ts:189-251 omit short-name aliases.
findings.recommendation: After resolving each declaration with realpathSync.native, derive its physical repository-relative path and repeat the protected-root/ancestor intersection check before granting sandbox or approval authority. Add repository-aware plan validation and a Windows regression using an available 8.3 alias such as `docs/EXEC-P~1/**`, asserting read-only fallback and approval denial.
findings.title: NTFS short-name aliases bypass protected task authority

findings.evidence: .agents/skills/devweave/scripts/devweave_v2/host_facade.py:139-155 prepares the gate intent, persists the acceptance mutation, and only afterward calls PlanStore.complete. plan_store.py:109 writes every mutation to the active path, while :162-165 exposes an after-replace crash boundary. A crash there leaves a status=completed plan under `docs/exec-plans/active` with an authoritative intent. run_git_coordinator.py:123-130 retries the intent using the completed control path but never performs the missing archive move; :329-348 therefore commits the active-path plan, after which checkpoint_proof.py:101-118 rejects it because completed state must be stored under `docs/exec-plans/completed`. The advanced HEAD and surviving intent remain unreconcilable. tests/test_v2_git_export.py:179-207 covers task after-replace recovery and :388-446 covers acceptance only after the archive move, leaving this acceptance-specific state-to-archive window untested.
findings.recommendation: Make acceptance lifecycle placement recoverable and idempotent: on reconciliation, move an active status=completed plan to its completed path before checkpointing, or persist the transition directly at the completed path. Add an acceptance fault test immediately after state replacement and before archive movement, then verify restart produces exactly one valid completed-path commit/ref/digest, a finalized journal, a clean tree, and an idempotent subsequent resume.
findings.title: Acceptance can become unrecoverable between state persistence and archive movement
